rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative resumes the God distinguished by the preceding signs; its distance signals exaltation and makes Him vivid after those attributes.
rows.anchor: واسم الإشارة موجه إلى من جرت عليه الصفات والأخبار السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing that God created humans, set their terms, and made the heavens and earth, the verse concludes that He alone is Lord and sovereign.
rows.anchor: فهو الرب دون غيره وهو الذي الملك والسلطان له لا لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qitmīr is the thin husk or thread in the groove of a date stone.
rows.anchor: والقطمير : القشرة التي في شق النواة كالخيط الدقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols own nothing, even something as slight as a qitmīr; since stone idols neither acquire nor receive property, they cannot be gods or intercessors.
rows.anchor: فإذا انتفى أنها تملك شيئا انتفى عنها وصف الإلهية بطريق الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional sentence is a second predicate of ‘those you invoke besides Him.’
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن تدعوهم } خبر ثان عن { الذين تدعون من دونه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that idols do not hear alerts polytheists to their incapacity; it is not itself the proof, since they believed the idols heard and addressed them with praise.
rows.anchor: والمقصد منها تنبيه المشركين إلى عجز أصنامهم بأنها لا تسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘even if they heard’ clause coordinates with the preceding clause; the waw is not parenthetical, and the hearing is hypothetical for argument’s sake.
rows.anchor: فإنها معطوفة على جملة { إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even supposing the idols heard, they would not answer or grant requests; repeated unanswered prayers before visible idols show incapacity or incomprehension, since their worshippers cannot be faulted as unworthy.
rows.anchor: فطالما دعوا الأصنام فلم يسمعوا منها جوابا وطالما دعوها فلم يحصل ما دعوها لتحصيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istijāba may mean answering a caller with words or granting a petitioner what was requested; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls this use of a shared word in both senses.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ما استجابوا } يجوز أن يكون بمعنى إجابة المنادي بكلمات الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same verb may also mean responding to a petitioner by giving the requested thing; he calls this use of a shared term in both meanings.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى إجابة السائل بتنويله ما سأله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse completes the exposure of idols by saying God will make them speak in the afterlife and disavow the worshippers’ association of them with God, including any invitation to or approval of idolatry.
rows.anchor: بأن تلك الأصنام ينطقها الله فتتبرأ من شركهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufr here means repudiation or denial accompanied by aversion.
rows.anchor: والكفر : جحد في كراهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive attributes the shirk to its human perpetrators: their associating the idols with God in divinity.
rows.anchor: والشرك أضيف إلى فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the idols by a rational relative pronoun and rational pronouns treats them as people, mockingly following the polytheists’ own framing.
rows.anchor: على تنزيل الأصنام منزلة العقلاء مجاراة للمردود عليهم على طريقة التهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing maxim authenticates the preceding reports: their speaker knows them and no one can inform the hearer as well.
rows.anchor: تذييل لتحقيق هذه الأخبار بأن المخبر بها هو الخبير بها وبغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ‘inform’ because nabaʾ denotes news of an important, momentous event.
rows.anchor: وعبر بفعل الإنباء لأن النبأ هو الخبر عن حدث خطير مهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is for anyone able to hear the saying: the sentence is cast as a general proverb rather than directed to one particular person.
rows.anchor: لأن هذه الجملة أرسلت مرسل الأمثال فلا ينبغي تخصيص مضمونها بمخاطب معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabīr is an intensive adjective from knowing something with certainty; it denotes the class of those truly expert in it.
rows.anchor: و { خبير } صفة مشبهة مشتقة من خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proverb’s brevity omits the objects of ‘inform’ and ‘expert’ and the dimension of likeness, all recoverable from context.
rows.anchor: فحذف منه متعلق فعل ( ينبىء ) ومتعلق وصف { خبير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the intended expert is the speaker, khabīr is indefinite to generalize under negation; denying any equal informer implies no one informs as he does, and identifies him through the maxim.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى : ولا ينبئك بهذا الخبر مثلي لأني خبرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathl means an equal in amount, hence ‘double,’ or an equal in quality, hence ‘similar’; the latter is a rare faʿl pattern for an active participle, like shibh, nidd, and khidn.
rows.anchor: والمثل بكسر الميم وسكون المثلثة : المساوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After abundant proofs and reminders fail to move the people and may feed their arrogance, the next address stresses God’s independence and that Islam will gain adherents who honor it.
rows.anchor: ناسب أن ينبئهم الله بأنه غني عنهم وأن دينه لا يعتز بأمثالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘People’ refers here to the polytheists, as is common Qur’anic usage, and to those addressed in the preceding passage.
rows.anchor: فالمراد ب { يا أيها الناس } هم المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminding them first of their dependence on God humbles them more than simply telling them He needs nothing from them; although they know their dependence, they miss its implications, so the reminder may awaken or convince them.
rows.anchor: وجه إليهم إعلام بأنهم الفقراء إلى الله لأن ذلك أدخل للذلة على عظمتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder may revive people whose sound minds were veiled by misguidance; even those remaining unbelievers will meet their lives with bewilderment and bitterness, unlike the praise of their ancestors and idols they had heard.
rows.anchor: فمن بقي على كفره كان بقاؤه مشوبا بحيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The defined subject and predicate restrict poverty to the addressed people relative to God, a restrictive reversal; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects a literal absolute restriction or an asserted hyperbolic reading as needless.
rows.anchor: فالوجه حمل القصر المستفاد من جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding al-Ḥamīd completes al-Ghanī and prevents the inference that divine independence excuses failure to worship; God is praised by those who worship and answer His call.
rows.anchor: فهو احتراس لدفع توهمهم أنه لما كان غنيا عن استجابتهم وعبادتهم فهم معذورون في أن لا يعبدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording balances their need ‘to God’ with His praise, and pairs their poverty with His wealth to show that divine wealth is joined to generosity.
rows.anchor: لأنه لما قيد فقرهم بالكون إلى الله قيد غنى الله تعالى بوصف { الحميد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 16–17 explain God’s independence: He could justly destroy the people and replace them with worshippers, but delays them through forbearance.
rows.anchor: فهو تعالى لغناه عنهم وغضبه عليهم لو شاء لأبادهم وأتى بخلق آخرين يعبدونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The will in context is a will arising from their deserving destruction; it does not refer to bare divine freedom, which needs no announcement.
rows.anchor: فالمشيئة هنا المشيئة الناشئة عن الاستحقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Taking away’ means destroying them from this world by a death that overtakes all of them, figuratively bringing them to the next world.
rows.anchor: والإذهاب مستعمل في الإهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A new creation means bringing into existence people who had neither existed nor been expected, namely people who believe in God.
rows.anchor: أي يوجد خلقا من الناس يؤمنون بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalq here means creatures, not the act of creating, as in the verse ‘This is God’s creation.’
rows.anchor: فالخلق هنا بمعنى المخلوق مثل قوله تعالى : { هذا خلق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The replacement threat echoes the promise that, if people turn away, God will substitute another people who will not be like them.
rows.anchor: وهذا في معنى قوله : { وإن تتولوا يستبدل قوما غيركم ثم لا يكونوا أمثالكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the reading that God merely hastens their deaths so their children’s generation can believe, since the statement that this is not difficult for God does not suit that interpretation.
rows.anchor: وليس المعنى : أنه إن يشأ يعجل بموتهم فيأتي جيل أبنائهم مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzīz means resistant or overpowering; saying the act is not difficult for God intensifies the warning.
rows.anchor: والعزيز : الممتنع الغالب ، وهذا زيادة في الإرهاب والتهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ‘wills’ is omitted because the conditional answer ‘He will remove you’ makes it clear; this ellipsis is common Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: ومفعول فعل المشيئة محذوف استغناء بما دل عليه جواب الشرط وهو { يذهبكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That’ points either to the removal implied by yudhhibkum or to the preceding matter construed as what was mentioned.
rows.anchor: والإشارة في قوله : { وما ذلك } عائدة إلى الإذهاب المدلول عليه ب { يذهبكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the threat, the text reassures Muslims that those who do no wrong will not bear a wrongdoer’s punishment, as in the promise to save the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: فعقب بأن من لم يأت وزرا لا يناله جزاء الوازر في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may also promise rescue from a worldly destruction that strikes the warned unbelievers, as at Badr; this special promise does not conflict with the warning that communal trials can affect the righteous too.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون وعدا بالإنجاء من عذاب الدنيا إذا نزل بالمهددين الإذهاب والإهلاك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Umm Salama asked whether a community would perish while righteous people were among them; the Prophet answered yes if evil became widespread.
rows.anchor: وما ورد في حديث أم سلمة قالت : ( يا رسول الله أنهلك وفينا الصالحون ؟ قال : نعم إذا كثر الخبث )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is called Ṣād after its first word; the letter name is spelled ṣād-alif-dāl, with its ending stopped on a sukūn when recited as a letter name.
rows.anchor: سميت في المصاحف وكتب التفسير وكتب السنة والآثار عن السلف ( سورة صاد )

rows.speaker: المعري
rows.claim: Al-Maʿarrī’s verse names the letter Ṣād; its kasra at the rhyme is a poetic change from the underlying sukūn, as in the line by Imruʾ al-Qays.
rows.anchor: وأما قول المعري يذكر سليمان عليه السلام

rows.speaker: السخاوي
rows.claim: Al-Sakhāwī reports from Jamāl al-Qurrāʾ that the sura is also called Sūrat Dāwūd, but gives no chain for that name.
rows.anchor: وفي ( الإتقان ) عن كتاب ( جمال القراء ) للسخاوي : أن سورة ص تسمى أيضا سورة داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name is written with the single glyph ṣād in the codex, following the spelling of other disconnected letters at sura openings.
rows.anchor: وكتب اسمها في المصاحف بصورة حرف الصاد مثل سائر الحروف المقطعة في أوائل السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is Meccan by general agreement; al-Jaʿbarī’s reported Medinan opinion conflicts with the consensus cited by several scholars, while al-Dānī’s Medinan opinion is explicitly judged unsound.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية في قول الجميع . وذكر في ( الإتقان ) أن الجعبري حكى قولا

rows.speaker: السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyūṭī says the Medinan attribution runs against the several scholars’ report of consensus that the sura is Meccan.
rows.anchor: قال السيوطي : وهو خلاف حكاية جماعة الإجماع على أنها مكية

rows.speaker: الداني
rows.claim: Al-Dānī records an opinion that the sura is Medinan but says it is not sound.
rows.anchor: وعن الداني في كتاب ( العدد ) قول بأنها مدنية وقال : إنه ليس بصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura came after al-Qamar and before al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: السورة الثامنة والثلاثون في عداد نزول السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse count is 86 for the people of the Ḥijāz, Syria, and Baṣra; Ayyūb ibn al-Mutawakkil al-Baṣrī counts 85, while Kūfa counts 88.
rows.anchor: وعدت آيها ستا وثمانين عند أهل الحجاز والشام والبصرة وعدها أيوب بن المتوكل البصري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed couplet contrasts the honor of a few protected by a powerful neighbor with the humiliation of the many, illustrating the sense of ʿizza.
rows.anchor: وما ضرنا أنا قليل وجارنا عزيز وجار الأكثرين ذليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fī is a metaphor of containment, conveying that they are deeply immersed in arrogance against the truth.
rows.anchor: و { في للظرفية المجازية مستعارة لقوة التلبس بالعزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shiqāq means obstinate opposition and quarrelling; here it is opposition to God through shirk and to His Messenger through denial.
rows.anchor: والشقاق : العناد والخصام . والمراد : وشقاق لله بالشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their inner arrogance and opposition are what prevent them from being moved by the Qur’anic reminder.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أن الحائل بينهم وبين التذكير بالقرآن هو ما في قرارة نفوسهم من العزة

words: كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of destroyed earlier peoples answers the implied question about the consequence of arrogance and opposition; it warns the present rejecters not to delay responding, since repentance at punishment will not help.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا البيان إخبارا مرفقا بحجة من قبيل قياس تمثيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is a parenthetic explanatory answer between the statement of arrogance and opposition and the report that they were astonished at a warner.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة معترضة بين جملة { بل الذين كفروا في عزة وشقاق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kamm is a noun denoting a large number; min qarn is its clarifying specification, and the whole phrase is the object of ‘We destroyed.’
rows.anchor: و { كم } اسم دال على عدد كثير . و { من قرن } تمييز لإبهام العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarn means a community, as in the verse about bringing other communities after them.
rows.anchor: والقرن : الأمة كما في قوله تعالى : { ثم أنشأنا من بعدهم قرونا آخرين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min qablihim may modify qarn as an adjective moved before it and thus functioning circumstantially, emphasizing that earlier peoples were their precedent in arrogance and destruction.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون ظرفا مستقرا جعل صفة ل { قرن } مقدمة عليه فوقعت حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, min qablihim may attach directly to ‘We destroyed’; its priority before the object gives it emphasis and hints that earlier peoples were destroyed for this stance.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون متعلقا ب { أهلكنا } على أنه ظرف لغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit label ‘the disbelievers’ replaces the expected pronoun to brand them as unbelievers in response to their branding the Prophet; kufr sums up corrupt thought and deeds.
rows.anchor: وهذا لقصد وصفهم بأنهم كافرون بربهم مقابلة لما وصموا به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to the Prophet and is used contemptuously, as in the question ‘Is this the one who mentions your gods?’
rows.anchor: أشاروا به إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم استعملوا اسم الإشارة لتحقير مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They uttered the accusation as they left the gathering at Abū Ṭālib mentioned in the sura’s occasion of revelation; their recent encounter made the Prophet seem present as they pointed to him.
rows.anchor: وإنما قالوا مقالتهم هذه حين انصرافهم من مجلس أبي طالب المذكور في سبب نزول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called incomprehensible claims such as one God or resurrection sorcery, since they associated magic with unintelligible speech, and called the understandable but impossible claim of prophethood a lie; they explain the charge through monotheism and the question of revelation.
rows.anchor: لأنهم لما لم تقبل عقولهم ما كلمهم به زعموا ما لا يفهمون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question explains their calling him a sorcerer and liar: they deem his report a false inversion of reality.
rows.anchor: فجملة { أجعل الآلهة إلها واحدا } بيان لجملة { هاذا ساحر كذاب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza conveys denial mixed with astonishment; they follow it with a statement that this is something astonishing.
rows.anchor: والهمزة للاستفهام الإنكاري التعجيبي ولذلك أتبعوه بما هو كالعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUjāb describes something greatly astonishing; the pattern faʿāl intensifies the quality, like ṭiwāl for very tall and kirām for very generous, stronger than karīm.
rows.anchor: و { عجاب } : وصف الشيء الذي يتعجب منه كثيرا لأن وزن فعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They attack the first of the three foundations of their unbelief, associating partners with God; the other two are rejecting the Messenger and denying resurrection and afterlife recompense.
rows.anchor: فإن أصول كفرهم ثلاثة : الإشراك ، وتكذيب الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intilāq literally means to depart and walk, but also serves as a verb of beginning because a person sets out toward an undertaking; the author compares dhahaba bi-fiʿl and the usage in a cited poem.
rows.anchor: ويستعمل استعمال أفعال الشروع لأن الشارع ينطلق إليه

rows.speaker: النبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Nabhānī’s line using dhahaba with a verb illustrates the analogous construction for a verb of beginning.
rows.anchor: فإن كنت سيدنا سدتنا وإن كنت للخال فاذهب فخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The use is compared with qāma in the account of the youths who stood and spoke in Sūrat al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قام في قوله تعالى : { إذ قاموا فقالوا في سورة الكهف }

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the chiefs actually left Abū Ṭālib’s gathering; he identifies ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ as the speaker.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : قائل ذلك عقبة بن أبي معيط

rows.speaker: غير ابن عطية
rows.claim: Other commentators name Abū Jahl, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, and al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth among those speaking.
rows.anchor: وقال غير ابن عطية : إن من القائلين أبا جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is explanatory: if intilāq is figurative for beginning, the chiefs began speaking; if it is literal departure, their exit after the prior debate implies discussion and planning, which the quoted command explains.
rows.anchor: و { أن } تفسيرية لأن الانطلاق إن كان مجازا فهو في الشروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Go on’ may mean literally leave the place of debate and remain firm in worship of your gods, or figuratively continue in your religion, like the idiom ‘walk as the noble walked.’
rows.anchor: والأمر بالمشي يحتمل أن يكون حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣabr is persistence and attachment, originally said of tying an animal; in hardship it means staying composed without panic.
rows.anchor: والصبر : الثبات والملازمة ، يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to remain steadfast in worship of the gods parallels the people’s claim that the Prophet nearly led them astray had they not persisted in their worship.
rows.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية قوله تعالى : { إن كاد ليضلنا عن آلهتنا لولا أن صبرنا عليها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlā conveys figurative establishment, as in ‘they are upon guidance’; unlike ṣabr ʿalā meaning patience with something, it means adhere to or remain in worship, with an implied noun ‘worship.’
rows.anchor: وحرف { على } يدل على تضمين { اصبروا } معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that this is a contrived matter meant for some ulterior purpose is intended to strengthen suspicion that the Prophet’s call is false.
rows.anchor: تعليل للأمر بالصبر على آلهتهم لقصد تقوية شكهم في صحة دعوة النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to what they heard at the gathering: the Prophet’s call to say there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: فالإشارة ب { هاذا } إلى ما كانوا يسمعونه في المجلس من دعوة النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘this’ in their denial refers to the same claim in the preceding accusation, namely making the many gods one.
rows.anchor: والإشارة إلى ما أشير إليه بقولهم : { إن هاذا لشيء يراد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence may stand independently or explain their claim that the matter is contrived, since saying they had never heard it shows they considered it invented.
rows.anchor: والجملة مستأنفة أو مبينة لجملة { إن هاذا لشيء يراد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the demonstrative instead of using a pronoun further distinguishes the claim; bi-hādhā has an omitted ‘like,’ meaning something like this.
rows.anchor: وإعادة اسم الإشارة من وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر لقصد زيادة تمييزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their report of never having heard this is a rhetorical way to express rejection and accuse the claim of falsehood.
rows.anchor: ونفي السماع هنا خبر مستعمل كناية عن الاستبعاد والاتهام بالكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Milla means religion, as shown by the verses about following the Jews’ and Christians’ religion and about the religion of Joseph’s forefathers.
rows.anchor: و { الملة } : الدين ، قال تعالى : { ولن ترضى عنك اليهود ولا النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ākhira is the feminine of ākhir, the one that comes after a period in which similar instances have been established, as in the later creation.
rows.anchor: و { الآخرة } : تأنيث الآخر وهو الذي يكون بعد مضي مدة تقررت فيها أمثاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase may be a circumstantial modifier of the demonstrative and attached to ‘heard’: they have never heard this before now, so do not accept it.
rows.anchor: والمجرور من قوله : { في الملة الآخرة } يجوز أن يكون ظرفا مستقرا في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأصحابه
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and his associates take the ‘last religion’ to mean Christianity; the polytheists invoked its plurality of gods against monotheism, and their denial of hearing this implies the opposite had been heard.
rows.anchor: وهو عن ابن عباس وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase can mean the Quraysh religion; at Abū Ṭālib’s deathbed the Prophet urged him to profess God’s oneness, while the chiefs asked whether he would abandon ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib’s religion.
rows.anchor: فقالوا له جميعا : أترغب عن ملة عبد المطلب
